correctness.rationale: All twelve conic-line intersections are proved rational and distinct in characteristic zero by their quadratic discriminants; all fifteen line-line intersections are rational. The eleven distinct singular points per model have verified profiles (6,3,2). Cross-product content prime supports are exhaustive exact arithmetic, giving all-prime stability outside 7,11 for the first model and outside 2,3,5 for the second. Exhaustive finite-field projective-point enumeration and local conic gradient analysis establish the two exceptional fibers. The standalone Python verifier derives all inputs and reproduces these certificates; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs. Char 7 reduced-support and char 11 tangency conventions are distinguished.

value.rationale: The first explicit rational weak Ziegler pair is a natural fixed arithmetic comparison object. A complete, not sampled, characteristic-reduction classification explains exactly where the two published integer presentations retain their seven smooth components and ordinary incidence structures. The exceptional fibers display qualitatively different nonroutine geometry: two line-pair coalescences at 7 versus a contact-two pair inside a four-branch singularity at 11; the other arrangement remains stable at every p>=7. This informs arithmetic use and specialization of this concrete benchmark without claiming a new Jacobian-syzygy theorem.
